Hi. My name is Ollie Akers. I'm 21 years old, and I have a little knack for curiosity. See, just last week, I was walking through the little forested area behind my home when I heard a cracking sound. It was quiet, barely loud enough to hear, but my head jerked straight towards the source. I walked towards it. I knew this forest like the back of my hand. Every tree, branch, path; I knew it all. Nobody else had the same connection I do with the Cyril Woods.

I pressed onwards. It was almost a minute since I heard the noise, and I was beginning to lose hope. I left wet footprints in my wake, after all, it had rained about thirty minutes prior. The ground was still soaking, and whatever cracked should have left some clues behind; a footprint, a smudge, something. After another minute of walking, I decided to give up. I must have moved past the source. I must have missed it. My curiosity got the better of me when my rationality should have overcome it, but I retraced my steps and looked even more. I couldn't stop looking for this cracking sound. It may have just been an animal, but I needed to know so badly.

Ten minutes passed. Then another ten. Soon, I had been out for an hour. Then two. I found nothing.

I checked my watch. It was nearly eight. The sun was setting soon. I began to head home, slightly distrought. After the eight minute trek home, I plumped onto my couch and flicked on the television. The six o'clock news was on, and they were reporting on something I never actually paid attention to because I nearly had a heart attack then and there.

"What, what?" I exclaimed. I hopped from the couch and looked at my watch. It was clearly past eight o'clock, but the television was airing the news from two hours ago. Something was fucked, and now I needed to know more than ever.

And I knew almost immediately after.

Before I continue with my story, I should tell you a bit more about myself. I'm 21, my birth name is Oliver, I haven't a girlfriend for over two years now, I dropped out of University last year to move into the house I live in now, and I like to think of myself as an adventurous fellow. Naturally curious, I want to explore the world, find out what I can, and hopefully start some kind of ridiculous journey. Or rather, I did. This is my memoir of sorts. The story I started to tell you previously happened to me about eight months ago. I hadn't had the time to write it all down, so I decided that today would be a good time to start.

Now, back to my home.

I knew almost immediately after.

I ran back outside. Something freaky was happening, and I needed to get to the bottom of it. I slowly drodged back to where I had first heard the cracking noise.

Sidenote again. Thinking about it now, maybe "snapping" isn't the best choice of a word. It was a popping or a snapping rather. I thought it was a branch, but in hindsight, the noise was less nature-ish than I initially wrote.

I laid to the ground, cheek-to-dirt. I wanted to find anything and everything that could have caused this fuckery to occur. I crawled over the where I first heart the popping noise. I saw torn up leaves by my footprints, smaller animal footsteps, and then a small chunk of rubber.

I sat upright, and grabbed this rubber. It was small, slightly smaller than a thumbnail, but it was rubber nonetheless. It looked like it came off a tire or boots. I took off my left boot and saw a small chunk of rubber was missing. That was quite odd. These were brand new boots, bought less than a month ago. They weren't already falling apart, were they? No, it looked like this piece of rubber was sliced off. As if a knife sliced through it. A slice to perfect to be deterioration.

Then, what could it be?

I laid backwards. The sun was actually beginning to set. My watch said 9:30, but it was apparently only 7:30 or so. I watched the sun move over the horizing, burning the sky a bright amber, then fading into darkness. The moon was exceptionally bright today. It was a full moon, and the stars were shinier than ever. That night was a beautiful sight. Ordinarily I would have laid down and stared at the stars for hours, but I suddenly felt a sharp pain in my right shoulder blade. A spasm of sorts.

I flipped around, and looked where I was laying. A small shard of glass was laying on the ground. There was some small smudges inside, some kind of purple dust or liquid, but it had since dried. It looked almost like a paintball. It was slightly dug into the ground, a shallow angle, but that angle was caused by more than my foot stepping on it. It seeped straight into the ground and probably caused that snap I heard.

But what the hell was this ball thing? I put a marker in the ground and sat back up. I did a rough estimation based off the angle it was in the ground. Wherever it came from, it was thrown or shot from about 20 meters. I made a perimeter of the area where this ball could have been shot from.

I walk along the line here, and notice a strange detail. There seemed to be a little burrowed nest under a tree. I reached in, and felt something inside. They were small egg-like objects. I grabbed a handful and pulled them out. They were all little glass balls, not much larger than a marble, and they had a variety of different colour liquids inside. Yellow, red, blue, green, and some were different consistencies, brightnesses, some were even so light they felt almost weightless, although gravity pulled them downwards in the same way as all the others. No matter how hard I tried, those lighter balls just didn't act as if they were light. They only felt that way.

"Now, what do these orbs actually do?" I wondered. I paused. "Orbs... I like that. Let's call these things Orbs."

And so it was.

Hey, sorry for another mid-anecdote side note, but It's like four in the morning here, I should probably go to bed. I'll continue telling writing in this journal tomorrow. It's been a long day, and trying to remember tiny details from eight months ago isn't exactly light on the brain. Anyways, good night.

I looked at this yellow orb I had picked up. Normal weight, wasn't too bright, but the colour intrigued me. I rolled it across the table. I rolled it back. I bounced it. Then I smashed it. Light flew out from the orb, stayed bright for a moment, and then it was dark again. The room was illuminated brightly for a brief moment of time, but not much else. I looked back into the back I held all the orbs. I reached inside, and out came another yellow.

I was sure that there was only one of every color.

I recounted. I was sure. There was only one yellow. There was no repeats of any of the colours. I smashed this yellow one. It glew brightly again. Then it dimmed. I reached inside my small pouch. I grabbed another orb. Another yellow.

As of that moment, I was not longer wondering if something screwy was going on, I knew something screwy was going on. I was then my goal to find out what it was.
